research.approach: Practitioners start from closed actuals in the ledger and measure every line against plan with one fixed sign convention and one materiality rule (a dollar floor and a percent, applied the same way every month). Before any variance means anything they make sure the ledger accounts roll up to the budget categories and that the report ties to the ledger's own profit and loss. They then trace only the lines over the threshold to the transactions behind them, mark each gap as timing (it reverses) or lasting (it changes the year), and carry only lasting gaps into a re-forecast. Each note says cause, timing or lasting, forecast effect and who owns the action.

steps.name: Pull month and year-to-date actuals from Xero and Gusto next to the budget
steps.why: Everything else rests on closed actuals for the same months as the budget.

steps.name: Map each ledger account to one budget category and tie the total back to Xero
steps.why: If the two do not line up, a variance may be a labelling difference, not spending. Mapping is the owner's stated unknown.

steps.name: Compute variance by category with one sign rule and one threshold
steps.why: Same rule every month makes months comparable; sort by dollars so the three biggest are clear.

steps.name: Trace the three biggest to transactions and mark each timing or lasting
steps.why: A cause nobody can show is a guess; timing gaps reverse and should not move the forecast.

steps.name: Re-forecast the year from lasting gaps and name an action and owner per gap
steps.why: Turns the report from a record into a decision tool.

steps.name: Lay out one page that reads in ten minutes and refresh it monthly
steps.why: Same layout each month; the owner learns where to look.

pitfalls.text: Chart of accounts and budget categories do not match, so a variance is really a classification gap.
Explaining every line instead of only those over a threshold, which buries the three that matter.
Treating a timing gap as lasting and moving the forecast, or the reverse.
Payroll booked gross in the ledger but exported net or by pay date from Gusto, so the two disagree for a reason that is not an error.

stages.name: Pin down the report
stages.goal: Turn the request into a measured outcome, the budget file, the months and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Put actuals and budget side by side
stages.goal: Pull Xero Profit and Loss by month, the Gusto payroll exports and the January budget into one working sheet.

checks.name: Revenue, total expenses and net profit for each month equal Xero's Profit and Loss for the same dates within $1
Budget totals by month equal the January spreadsheet's own totals exactly
Payroll cost by month from Gusto agrees with the ledger payroll accounts within 2%, or the gap is explained (for example pay date versus accrual)

stages.name: Check accounts map to budget categories
stages.goal: Map each Xero account with a balance to exactly one budget category and say whether the two structures match.

checks.name: Every account with a balance maps to exactly one budget category; none is split or left out without a note
Unmapped or ambiguous accounts are under 2% of total expenses, or each is listed for the owner
Mapped category totals still equal Xero's total expenses within $1 (nothing lost or counted twice)
Ends with MATCHES, PARTLY or DOES NOT MATCH and what that means for the variances

stages.name: Find and explain the three biggest variances
stages.goal: Compute variance by category, pick the three biggest gaps in dollars, trace each to transactions and mark each timing or lasting.

outputs.name: Variance table and the three explained

checks.name: One sign rule (actual minus budget; expense above budget unfavourable) and one threshold (a dollar floor and a percent, agreed before running) are written at the top and used for every line
Category variances add up to the net profit variance within $1
Each of the three has at least one named transaction, invoice or payroll run behind it, or says cause unknown
Each of the three is marked timing or lasting with the test used (for example gap reverses in the next month, or year-to-date gap is under half the month gap)
Every listed hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with evidence

stages.name: Re-forecast the year and rank actions
stages.goal: Carry only lasting gaps into a re-forecast of the year, then propose an action, an owner and an expected dollar effect for each of the three variances.

checks.name: The re-forecast moves only for gaps marked lasting; timing gaps are shown but do not change the year
Each action cites its variance, expected dollar effect, effort, confidence and who owns it
The re-forecast equals actuals to date plus the remaining budget, adjusted; the arithmetic is shown and totals tie to the diagnosis

stages.name: Owner chooses what to do about each gap
stages.goal: The owner picks an action for each of the three variances and confirms the account-to-category map. Record the reason when a top action is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over actions are in decisions.jsonl
The owner has confirmed or corrected every ambiguous account in the map

stages.name: Build the one-page report and the monthly refresh
stages.goal: Build the Google Sheet tabs: mapped actuals, budget, and a one-page report with the headline, category table, the three explained variances and the chosen actions. Save the steps to refresh it each month.

checks.name: The report fits one printed page and has no more than 400 words outside the tables
Every figure on the page matches the diagnosis and Xero's Profit and Loss within $1
The refresh steps were rerun on the prior month's data and gave the same layout and a result that ties to Xero

stages.name: Check last month's forecast against what happened
stages.goal: Once the next month closes in Xero, compare the re-forecast and the explanations with closed actuals and say whether the report is earning its place.

checks.name: Forecast and actuals use the same categories, map and Xero closed figures
Forecast error is shown per category; any line off by more than 10% and over the dollar floor is explained
No verdict is given on the forecast until at least two months have closed; before that it says INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep the rules and plan next month
stages.goal: Save the threshold, sign rule and mapping as rules, list what the next run needs, and set how last month's re-forecast will be compared with actuals.

checks.name: Each saved rule says whether it holds for this report, this business or the playbook
Next run lists the inputs to export, the date they are needed and the re-forecast comparison to make

hypotheses.statement: Some variances are labelling differences because Xero accounts do not match the budget categories.
hypotheses.test: Map every account with a balance and count dollars in accounts that map to no category or to more than one.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 5% of expense dollars sit in unmapped or ambiguous accounts.
hypotheses.refute_if: Under 2% of expense dollars are unmapped and category totals tie to Xero.

hypotheses.statement: The biggest gaps are timing (annual bills, late invoices, pay dates) and reverse soon.
hypotheses.test: Compare the month gap with the year-to-date gap and with the next month's gap for each of the three.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The year-to-date gap is under half the month gap, or the gap reverses the next month.
hypotheses.refute_if: The year-to-date gap is as large as or larger than the month gap.

hypotheses.statement: Payroll (hiring, overtime, bonuses or contractors) drives most of the expense variance.
hypotheses.test: Compare Gusto payroll cost by month with the budgeted payroll lines and with headcount.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Payroll lines account for more than 40% of the total expense variance.
hypotheses.refute_if: Payroll is within the threshold and other lines carry the variance.

hypotheses.statement: Revenue, not cost, drives the gap between budget and actual profit.
hypotheses.test: Compare revenue variance with the net profit variance.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Revenue variance is more than half of the net profit variance.
hypotheses.refute_if: Revenue is within the threshold of budget.

hypotheses.statement: The January budget is out of date, so the same lines miss every month.
hypotheses.test: Check whether the same lines carry a variance of the same sign in each closed month of the year.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The same line is more than 10% off budget, in the same direction, in at least 3 closed months.
hypotheses.refute_if: Variances change sign or size from month to month.

hypotheses.statement: One-off or miscoded transactions inflate a line.
hypotheses.test: List the largest transactions in each of the three lines and check vendor history and category.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A single transaction accounts for more than half of a line's variance, or sits in an unusual category for that contact.
hypotheses.refute_if: The variance is spread over many ordinary transactions.

measurement.window: Each month, once Xero closes, compare the previous re-forecast with closed actuals for the same lines.
measurement.min_volume: At least two closed months before judging the re-forecast.
measurement.stop_rule: No live changes are made; if actuals fail to tie to Xero within $1, fix the mapping before reporting.
